source_document.body:
Truckload carriers that can’t dispatch a truck for a tendered load now have somewhere to send it besides back to the shipper. Graypool , the Atlanta freight software company formerly known as HOPTEK, opened Graypool Exchange on Wednesday. It launched with seven founding member carriers, which pass qualified freight directly to one another.
The exchange runs inside the tender software Graypool already operates for its carriers. When a member can’t put a truck on a load it wants to keep, the system can offer that load to other members before the carrier rejects it. Each member sets which freight it will offer, which it will take, and at what price.
The launch comes as carriers turn away far more contract freight than a year ago. Third-quarter tender rejections averaged 14.5%, up from 5.3% a year earlier, according to the SONAR Truckload Rejection Index . Rejections have since eased to 12.77% in the index’s latest weekly reading, the lowest since early May.
“Across the U.S., truckload carriers turn away freight they want every day, not because the lane is wrong, but because the truck is,” Graypool CEO Marc Held said in the release. “Until now, carriers have had no venue of their own to send it to.”
What happens to a rejected tender today
When a carrier rejects a tender, the shipper offers the load to the next carrier in its routing guide . Each step down that list costs more. Shippers paid 9.25% more for loads accepted on the second tender, according to SONAR’s Routing Guide Premiums index when it launched in late October. Loads that slid to the third tender or beyond cost 19.84% more.
The exchange gives the first carrier another option, Held said in an interview with FreightWaves. A shipper offers Carrier A a load at $100. If Carrier A has no truck in position but Carrier B will run it for $80, Carrier A keeps the shipper and $20 of margin . Carrier B gets freight it could not otherwise reach.
“It gives them the ability to always say yes, because the one thing that a carrier always wants to do is when someone says, ‘Hey, will you move this from point A to point B?’ They always want to say yes. Period,” Held said. “The thing that we are just enabling them to do is making it so that they can say yes profitably.”
Seven members, by invitation only
The exchange is open to carriers by invitation. Members operate under shared commercial, data, and insurance standards, with interchange agreements approved by their insurers, according to the release. Only loads whose shippers allow a hand-off reach the exchange. Freight a shipper requires its contracted carrier to run never gets there.
Graypool runs the exchange, holds no freight of its own, and takes no side in a trade. “We don’t take the load. We don’t broker it. We run the floor,” Held said in the release.
Because Graypool already decides which loads fit each carrier’s network, the system can ask every member at once whether it wants a load, Held said. The answer has to come back in under five seconds.
“There is no separate load board where a carrier needs to bid on these assets again,” he said. “We’re already doing that.”
Paper Transport, a Graypool customer, backed the exchange in the release. “Graypool Exchange is our first choice for finding capacity we can trust and freight from respected partners,” said Ben Schill, corporate development officer at Paper Transport.
Graypool’s existing carrier business
The exchange is Graypool’s third product. Graypool Accept decides which tendered freight enters a carrier’s network, and Graypool Source finds and bids on spot freight . Graypool said carriers have booked $150 million in annualized freight revenue through Source.
Graypool’s customers include Werner, Marten, Prime, Hirschbach, Paper Transport, and Maybach International Group. The company raised $5 million in pre-seed funding from Jerk Ventures, Kearney, LPX Partners, Venture 53, and Werner Enterprises when it dropped the HOPTEK name in October.
But the exchange starts small. Shippers do not send freight to it directly, Held said. It works off the contract tenders and spot loads Graypool already handles for its carriers.
Held compares Graypool to exchange operators such as Nasdaq and Intercontinental Exchange. “I think the magic is in actually turning these over-the-counter marketplaces into a single clearing house,” he said.
Why it matters: Asset carriers bidding on 2027 contract freight can commit to lanes their own trucks won’t always reach, provided other members cover the gaps. That math gets sharper if rejections hold above 12% through January, which a FreightWaves SONAR analysis says would make double-digit contract increases the base case.
